timeline.message:
Windows, JNI: rewrite CreateJunction

In this PR:

- replace custom JunctionDescription definition
  with REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER from MSDN

- clean up kMaxJunctionTargetLen computation

- use already-computed offsets when creating the
  PathBuffer

Motivation:

- I'm implementing readSymbolicLink. It should
  handle junctions as well as symlinks. (There can
  be pre-existing symlink created from Admin
  shells, or the user may have enabled
  unprivileged symlink creation.)

- REPARSE_DATA_BUFFER contains structs in a union
  for junction and symlink data, and is the
  idiomatic struct definition to work with
  FSCTL_SET_REPARSE_POINT/FSCTL_GET_REPARSE_POINT.

See https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7907
timeline.author: Laszlo Csomor

timeline.message:
Windows: implement readSymbolicLink

In this PR:

- Implement ReadSymlinkOrJunction in the JNI
  library, and expose it to Java code. This method
  can resolve symlinks and junctions.

- Override readSymbolicLink in WindowsFileSystem
  and use the new native method

- Add unit tests to exercise junction resolution.
  Manual testing shows the code works for symlinks
  too, however we cannot reliably create them in
  tests because that requires unprivileged symlink
  creation support (i.e. for the test to run as
  Admin, or for the OS having enabled it)

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7907
timeline.author: Laszlo Csomor

timeline.body:
In this PR:

- Implement ReadSymlinkOrJunction in the JNI
  library, and expose it to Java code. This method
  can resolve symlinks and junctions.

- Override readSymbolicLink in WindowsFileSystem
  and use the new native method

- Add unit tests to exercise junction resolution.
  Manual testing shows the code works for symlinks
  too, however we cannot reliably create them in
  tests because that requires unprivileged symlink
  creation support (i.e. for the test to run as
  Admin, or for the OS having enabled it)

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/7907
This PR is ready, but depends on https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/7928.
Why comment here? Is `READ_SYMLINK_OR_JUNCTION_ERROR` set or used anywhere?

reply.body:
For documentation, and to indicate that the value exists. The variable is not used anywhere (handled by `switch.default`).

Removed.

timeline.body:
Very nice! Thanks!

- We also have similar logic in https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/53156db1e30fe7197889c3cbc8d1321ff9b85143/src/main/cpp/util/file_windows.cc#L464
Should we refactor it to use `ReadSymlinkOrJunction` ?

- I think we can assume our CI system support creating symlink and also add tests for symlink. And we can give clear message when creating symlink fails so that people run the test locally know why.

Thanks for the pointer. Yes, I'll refactor `src/main/cpp/util/file_windows.cc`.

I'd rather not expect symlink support in tests. I tend to run tests locally, and I have symlinks disabled (to emulate users' environment).

reply.body: These values match constants in `src/main/native/windows/file.h`. Added comments.

timeline.body: OK, I am fine with skipping the test for symlink in this change. But I think, eventually, we should have a `windows_symlink_test` somewhere, then maybe tag it as `symlink_required` so that users can filter it if their local machine doesn't support symlink.

+        },
+    )
